name: Central Dili
tagline: The waterfront, the Government Palace and the offices
description: The strip along the seafront from the Government Palace east, holding the ministries, the international organisations, the better hotels and most of the restaurants. It is flat, walkable and where the country's institutional life is concentrated.
bestFor: Anyone working with government, the United Nations or the aid sector
pros: The whole professional network is here
Best internet and accommodation in the country
cons: The most expensive part of Dili
Built for institutions rather than residents

name: Farol and Motael
tagline: The western districts, embassies and the sea
description: The residential districts west of the centre along the coast, with the embassies, the Motael church that was a focus of resistance during the occupation, and much of the housing the international community uses. It is quieter and greener than the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the coast and the diplomatic quarter
cons: A vehicle or microlet is needed

name: Cristo Rei and Areia Branca
tagline: The eastern headland with the statue and the beach
description: The coast running east from the city to the headland where the Cristo Rei statue stands, reached by a long flight of steps, with Areia Branca beach below it. It is the closest good swimming to the capital and where Dili exercises.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a beach and a run within reach of the city
pros: Areia Branca and Dolok Oan beaches
The Cristo Rei steps and the view
Quieter and greener than central Dili
cons: Fifteen minutes east of the centre

name: Comoro and Bairro Pite
tagline: The working districts west, with the airport
description: The dense residential and commercial districts west of the centre towards the airport, with the Timor Plaza mall, the markets and most of Dili's ordinary housing. It is where the majority of the city's population actually lives.
bestFor: Long stays at local prices with the airport nearby
pros: Much cheaper than the coastal districts
Timor Plaza and the local markets

name: Atauro Island
tagline: The island offshore with the most biodiverse water on earth
description: An island about thirty kilometres north of Dili, reached by ferry in a couple of hours or by fast boat in less, whose surrounding waters a 2016 survey found to have the highest average reef fish diversity ever recorded anywhere.
bestFor: Divers and anyone whose reason for coming is the reef
pros: The most biodiverse reef waters ever surveyed
cons: A ferry or boat trip from Dili
